register.name: Flash Appeal for the Occupied Palestinian Territory 2026
register.detail: Published 16 December 2025 · For 2026 · Gaza $3.72 billion · West Bank $351.2 million · 201 partners
register.note: 3.62 million people in need; 2.97 million targeted
register.text: The 2026 appeal of 201 UN agencies, international and national NGOs and the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement for Gaza and the West Bank. It finances food assistance, health and nutrition, water and sanitation, shelter, education, cash and protection. It reaches food, water, shelter, education and health.

register.name: UNRWA occupied Palestinian territory Flash Appeal 2026
register.detail: For 2026 · Gaza and the West Bank
register.note: Emergency assistance for Palestine refugees in Gaza and the West Bank
register.text: The 2026 emergency appeal of UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestine refugees, for Gaza and the West Bank. In Gaza it finances food and emergency cash, primary health care and nutrition, water and sanitation, temporary learning spaces, collective shelters and cash-for-work; in the West Bank, cash for shelter and basic needs, food, education and emergency health. It reaches food, water, shelter, education, health and livelihood.

register.name: Palestinian Fund for Reconstruction and Development (PFRD)
register.detail: World Bank multi-donor trust fund · $241 million mobilised as of September 2026 · 92% of paid-in funds committed
register.note: Canada, France, Iceland, Japan, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom
register.text: The World Bank restructured the PURSE multi-donor trust fund into the PFRD at the Palestinian Authority’s request. Its objective is to strengthen sustainable recovery and reconstruction, economic recovery and social resilience in the West Bank and Gaza. It is a pooled fund: the source names no single standard.

register.name: Replenishment of the World Bank program for the West Bank and Gaza
register.detail: Approved by the Board of Executive Directors 30 June 2026
register.note: Gaza early recovery, West Bank services and jobs, and fiscal support
register.text: A $300 million replenishment of the World Bank’s program for the West Bank and Gaza. It supports an integrated multi-sectoral early recovery program in Gaza, subject to Board endorsement of the resumption of activities; investments in essential services and job creation in the West Bank; and fiscal support. It reaches livelihood through job creation.

register.name: Palestinian Partnership for Infrastructure Development Multi-Donor Trust Fund (PID MDTF)
register.detail: Launched 2012 · 18 investment operations co-financed, eight active · Nine partners
register.text: A World Bank multi-donor trust fund for Palestinian infrastructure that has channelled $299 million since its launch in 2012. Its current allocations include $5 million for integrated solid waste management and $5 million for ASPIRE 3, an energy operation. It reaches energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Solar Power Field Project
register.detail: Signed 19 June 2026, IsDB Group Annual Meetings, Baku · Two plants, 20 MW, with 55 MWh of storage
register.note: Total project cost $37 million, with other funders and the Palestinian government
register.text: An agreement with the Islamic Development Bank for two solar power plants with a total capacity of 20 megawatts and 55 megawatt-hours of energy storage, implemented through the Palestinian Energy and Natural Resources Authority. It reaches energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: EU Palestine facility for local banks
register.detail: 8 June 2026 · Bank of Palestine $150M · Quds Bank $100M · Palestine Investment Bank $70M · The National Bank $50M · Cairo Amman Bank $25M · €2.1M technical assistance
register.note: Part of the European Commission’s recovery and resilience programme
register.text: Five sub-loans to local banks, part structured as sub-debt to strengthen their capital base, through which the Palestine Monetary Authority directs credit to Palestinian micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It aims to sustain business activity and jobs. It reaches livelihood.

register.name: Urgent Program to Support the Palestinian People, twenty-third phase
register.detail: Approved by the Board of Governors, April 2025 · 124 proposed projects
register.note: Grants; about KD 307.1 million from the Arab Fund to Palestine since 1974
register.text: A grant programme of the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development for the Palestinian people. Its funds go to rural development (38.7%), associations and civil institutions (21.0%), education (16.6%), health (15.6%) and economic empowerment (6.4%). It reaches education, health and livelihood.
by: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development

register.name: French support for rural communities in Area C
register.detail: Signed 17 November 2026 · Near Tubas and Salfit, West Bank · About 22,000 people by early 2027
register.note: Signed by the French Consulate General, AFD and the ministries of finance and local government
register.text: A French grant to build and improve water, sanitation, electricity and health services and to support farming and crafts in rural communities near Tubas and Salfit, in Area C of the West Bank. About 22,000 people are expected to benefit by early 2027. It reaches water, shelter, energy, health and livelihood.

register.name: Programme for Emergency Recovery (Phase 3)
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 10 November 2026, Ramallah · Gaza Strip and the West Bank
register.note: Maximum amount; equipment for solid waste, debris removal and road and land rehabilitation
register.text: A Japanese grant, signed by the Minister of Finance and Planning and JICA, that procures equipment and materials for emergency recovery in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank: solid waste management, debris removal, and road and land rehabilitation. Its objective is to restore living conditions and strengthen public services. It reaches shelter, through the clearing and rehabilitation of land for rebuilding.

register.name: Team Gaza Initiative
register.detail: Launched 13 July 2026, Palestine Donor Group, Brussels · European Commission, 13 governments, the EIB and the World Bank
register.text: An initiative that brings together €883.6 million of financial contributions from the European Commission, 13 governments, the European Investment Bank and the World Bank for early recovery in Gaza. It supports water and sanitation, debris removal, health, energy, and agriculture and food systems. It reaches water, energy, health and food.

register.name: PEGASE support to the Palestinian Authority, 2026 and 2027
register.detail: €310 million committed by the European Commission for 2026 and 2027 · €41.7 million of Member State contribution agreements signed 13 July 2026
register.note: €3.8 billion channelled through PEGASE since its creation in 2008
register.text: PEGASE, created by the EU in 2008, has channelled €3.8 billion of support to the Palestinian people. The European Commission committed €310 million through it for 2026 and 2027, and Member States signed €41.7 million of new contribution agreements on 13 July 2026. It is budget-wide support: the source names no single standard.

register.name: TAJDID: wastewater treatment and agricultural reuse in Jenin West
register.detail: Agreements announced 6 May 2026 · EU and AFD €5.5M · KfW €11.2M · Jenin Governorate
register.note: About 36,000 residents of five towns in the first phase
register.text: A wastewater treatment plant, more than 100 km of collection networks and the safe reuse of treated wastewater in agriculture in Jenin West, co-financed by the EU, AFD and KfW, with emergency repairs to damaged water and wastewater systems. It reaches shelter, through safely managed sanitation, as well as water and food.

register.name: Programme for Emergency Recovery (Phase 2)
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 15 February 2026 · Gaza Strip and the West Bank
register.note: Maximum amount; equipment for solid waste, electricity, medical and water services
register.text: A Japanese grant that provides equipment for solid waste management, electricity, medical services, water services and basic infrastructure in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, for recovery and reconstruction. It reaches energy, health and water.

register.name: Saudi grant to the Palestinian Authority
register.text: A grant from Saudi Arabia to the Palestinian Authority, reported on 2 December 2025. It is budget-wide: the source names no single standard.

register.name: Multiannual and Comprehensive Programme to support Palestine’s Recovery and Resilience
register.detail: Adopted by the European Commission, April 2025 · Covers three years
register.note: The EU facility for local banks is part of it
register.text: The European Commission’s €1.6 billion programme, adopted in April 2025, to support Palestine’s recovery and resilience over three years. The EU facility for local banks is part of it. It is budget-wide: the source names no single standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 37.6% are under fifteen, and nine in ten young people complete lower secondary school: an educated generation.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Farms, olive groves and orchards across nearly two thirds of the land.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Bethlehem, Jericho and Hebron: places of pilgrimage for the world.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Canaan Palestine
items.text: Buys olives from more than 2,400 family farms across the West Bank at premiums above the average market rate, and sells its organic, fair trade olive oil and foods in more than 600 US retailers.

items.name: Flowless
items.text: A Ramallah-based social enterprise that uses technology to help water utilities and farmers manage water, and a finalist of the 2024 Continuum Spark Awards.

items.name: Comet-ME
items.text: Brings solar micro-grids, solar home systems, safe water and internet to off-grid Palestinian villages, serving over 11,000 people in 131 communities across the West Bank.

items.name: FATEN
items.text: The largest microfinance institution in the West Bank and Gaza, with 34 branches and nearly 24,000 borrowers, lending to small businesses and women-led firms with EBRD loans.

items.name: BuildPalestine
items.text: Builds skills, partnerships and values-aligned capital for Palestinian social entrepreneurs in Gaza and the West Bank, having mobilised $1.2 million for more than 30 enterprises in nine years.
